newsitem.title: JAPAN: MARK BATTERED IN TOKYO, SETS TWO-YEAR LOW VS YEN.
newsitem.headline: MARK BATTERED IN TOKYO, SETS TWO-YEAR LOW VS YEN.

text.p: 0620 GMT TRADED HIGH/LOW AS OF 0600 GMT

The German mark slumped in Tokyo on Thursday, setting a fresh two-year low of 62.73 yen, following worsening German jobs data on Wednesday and amid continued concerns about Europe's single currency, dealers said.
The dollar briefly rose against the yen in afternoon trade on worries about the health of Japanese construction firms, but fears of a U.S.-Japan trade dispute limited its gains.
The mark recovered against the dollar and the yen in late trade overseas on Wednesday, but that gave speculators and Japanese exporters a good chance to sell marks, traders said.
"There was constant selling in the mark, basically in line with recent trends," said a dealer at Long-Term Credit Bank of Japan Ltd.
Many traders expect the dollar to continue its upward march against the mark to 1.89 or 1.90 marks, while the yen could also strengthen further against the German currency.
The mark, quoted around 62.69/72 yen at 0638 GMT, was on the brink of hitting fresh lows, dealers said.

Japanese exporters who have lagged in selling marks against the yen were said to be keen to sell into any mark rallies. But they could be forced to swallow currency losses, dealers said, when they convert their marks into yen.
"Sixty yen (against the mark) will be in our sights if the mark breaks decisively below 62.50 yen," said Yoh Nihei, a manager at Sakura Bank.

A bank dealer said the mark's direction in the near term could be affected by the performance of sterling, with the market closely focusing on the Bank of England's decision on interest rates at its monetary meeting later in the day.

"If the BOE raises its interest rate, that could spark buying of sterling versus the mark and then prompt mark selling against the dollar," said the bank dealer. He said the chances of a rate increase were fifty-fifty.

The dollar/yen came under selling pressure from the yen's rise against the mark and the topside was weighted at around 118.90 yen due to traders' willingness to unload long positions established above 119.00 yen on Wednesday.
Remarks by U.S. Trade Representative Charlene Barshefsky also made operators cautious of pushing the dollar too high ahead of Friday's release of Japan's June current account data.
Barshefsky told reporters on Wednesday that Japan should not rely too much on exports to improve its economy and expressed disappointment about the recent sharp fall in U.S. auto sales in Japan.
Economists' forecasts for Japan's June current account surplus ranged from 840 billion yen to 1.1 trillion yen.
The data will be released at 8.50 a.m. Friday (2350 GMT Thursday).
"Since U.S. voices over Japan's trade surplus have been getting louder, we have to watch out carefully for the trade data," said a Japanese bank dealer.

The 225-share Nikkei average closed down 226.22 points or 1.15 percent at 19,475.85. It briefly slid as low as 19,366.14. Shares of debt-burdened construction firms tumbled and some hit record lows as investors rushed to cut their losses.
This supported the dollar against the yen on its falls, dealers said.
The dollar closed at 118.69/74 yen and 1.8820/30 marks in New York on Wednesday.
